record.tranche_reason: The post compares selected safety-relevant features across SAE dictionary sizes and reports that most did not recur in a related form, qualifying the consistency of cross-size feature correspondence.
record.gate_note: The post's own result is a tally matching selected 1M SAE safety features to the 34M SAE. It does not test whether matched features partition inputs or point in nearby directions. Excluded figures and measurements quoted from Anthropic's report, and proposed future tests.
record.test_reason: The post's only own result is a manual tally: do 22 published 1M-SAE safety features have a 'related form' among published 34M-SAE features of Claude 3 Sonnet? That measures cross-size feature recurrence, not splitting. It does not check whether finer features cover a coarse feature's inputs, lie near its direction, form families, absorb parents, or decompose into smaller-SAE latents. A 'None' match may only mean the feature is missing from Anthropic's non-exhaustive published examples, as a commenter notes, so the tally cannot show the absence of split or related features. Recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author takes the 7/22 recurrence as evidence that SAEs lack a consistent set of features they find. He says whether an important feature is found may depend on the training seed, or the SAE may be biased against it. He does not himself caveat the tally as selected; that caveat comes from a commenter.
record.recipe_differences: The post does not train SAEs or reproduce the original measurement; it manually compares selected published feature descriptions across two SAE dictionary sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: By the author's manual count, 7 of 22 published 1M-SAE safety-relevant features have a related published 34M-SAE feature; 15 have none found. Several matches are narrower (e.g., 'weapons or drugs' to 'how to make drugs').
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs of different dictionary sizes on the same model do not consistently recover the same (safety-relevant) features.

record.problems: The tally covers only 22 selected safety-relevant features, and the post does not state a systematic matching procedure or independently verify missed correspondences.

untested.parts: All: replacement of coarse features by finer ones covering inputs and near in direction.
All: split structure in large models or open SAE releases; the tally does not measure splitting.
All: nested, geometrically close families mirroring a hierarchy.
All: absorption and its insensitivity to SAE size or sparsity.
All: decomposition of larger latents into smaller ones and novel latents; the recurrence tally does not measure these.
All: objective-driven origin of splitting and alternative objectives.

record.verdict_notes: This is a commentary post on Scaling Monosemanticity. Its other content (correlation simulation, comments on activation distributions) does not bear on splitting. The linked code is a correlation simulator, not code for the tally. The matching procedure is unstated and the comparison set is likely non-exhaustive.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a coarse feature is replaced by finer features that partition its inputs and lie near its direction.
The tally compares selected features across 1M and 34M SAEs for Claude 3 Sonnet; it does not test split structure, input coverage, feature directions, other large models, or open SAE releases.
Nested feature families, geometric closeness, and whether they mirror a concept hierarchy.
Parent-child co-firing, absorption, and effects of changing SAE size or sparsity on absorption.
Whether larger latents decompose into combinations of smaller latents or whether larger SAEs add novel latents.
Whether splitting is caused by the SAE objective or changes under alternative objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: Claude 3 Sonnet
rows.operation_detail: Manually tallied whether selected 1M SAE safety-relevant features had a corresponding feature in related form in the 34M SAE.
rows.measure: Count of selected 1M SAE features recurring in related form in the 34M SAE
rows.locator: Finding Specific Features; tally of More Safety Relevant Features
rows.note: The author presents this as their own tally and describes the matching criterion as recurrence in a related form.
rows.check: Measures whether a feature recurs 'in some related form' across dictionary sizes, not splitting structure, input coverage or direction. The 34M candidates appear to come from Anthropic's published, non-exhaustive feature examples, so 15/22 'None' cannot be read as no successor or child features. Linking to V2 with state partial overstates what the row shows.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
